findings.rule: re-verification of round 0 blocking finding (traceback on malformed config)
findings.evidence: I ran CliRunner probes on the working tree and on HEAD extracted with git archive, both on the same make_root project. There were 17 configs: invalid YAML, non-UTF-8, a directory, a non-dict top level, bool/list/blank review_model, bool/400-digit/string/null/.inf/250000 budgets, a review_reviewers map or int, and a missing config. Each config ran 16 commands: delivery lane with and without --model, delivery review prepare and verify, revision open and close, goal render spec-plan/spec-implement/spec-fix/spec-status, validate --progression implement and clarify, pipeline next and update, and validate --prepare-review. No combination produces a traceback in 093. HEAD had a traceback for lane without --model and for render spec-implement without --model on the three unreadable configs. Invalid YAML, non-UTF-8 and directory configs now give review_config_invalid: exit 2 for lane, prepare, verify and render, exit 1 for progression, pipeline update and revision open. A HEAD-rendered spec-plan goal whose config later breaks or goes out of bounds is refused cleanly at refresh by goal prove (exit 2, recompile failed: review_config_invalid / review_max_chars_out_of_bounds). The blocking finding is fixed for every caller.

An unresolved identity never passes. goal_delivery_lane (identity_required=False) appends the identity error as a reason, so the lane is full (probes: spec-implement --model=default gives full [review_model_required]; --review-max-chars=200001 or 999 gives full [review_max_chars_out_of_bounds]). progression_gate turns ReviewIdentityError into ProgressionBlocked. revision._reviews returns the error code, so a revision stays open. goal_generic_evidence._delivery_review_missing_items catches it as a ValueError and reports a missing item. The other prepare_feature_review callers (orchestrator, review_api, semantic_analysis, acceptance_review, revision_commit, clarify_io/review_io through validate) catch ValueError or Exception.

The new module-level `from .goal_compile import normalize_goal_flags` makes `python -c 'import validator.goal_review_identity'` fail with `ImportError: cannot import name '_compile_command_goal' from partially initialized module 'validator.goal_compile'`. It imported fine at HEAD. The goal_compile <-> goal_contracts cycle already existed: `import validator.goal_compile` fails alone in both trees. The only importer, goal_recompile, loads goal_contracts first, so validator.cli, goal_recompile and goal_cli_actions import fine and nothing breaks at runtime. The new edge still makes the module depend on import order.
findings.correction: Import normalize_goal_flags lazily inside flag_budget, as ReviewIdentityError already is, or import it from goal_contracts if it is re-exported there.

findings.evidence: flag_budget accepts any ASCII digit string and calls int(). With `--flags --review-max-chars=<5000 nines>`, `goal render spec-plan|spec-implement|spec-status` ends in an uncaught `ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion`. HEAD tracebacks the same way, so this is not a regression, but the r1 correction was meant to make this flag refuse cleanly. The same int() is in delivery/goal.py:23.
findings.correction: Refuse budgets longer than len(str(REVIEW_MAX_CHARS_MAX)) digits (or wrap int() in try/except ValueError) and raise ReviewIdentityError('review_max_chars_out_of_bounds', ...).

findings.rule: spec 093 AC-001 / edge case 'blank values name no model'
findings.evidence: With `--flags --model=` (empty value), bind_review_model gets supplied='' and resolves the configured model. It then recompiles with [..., '--model=', '--model=reviewer/v1'], but goal_payload._bind_task_review_identity takes the first --model= flag. The probe shows that `goal render spec-plan --flags --model=` exits 0 and binds reviewer_model '' on the review tasks instead of the configured 'reviewer/v1'. HEAD behaves identically, so this is not a regression. At proof time a semantic review task with model '' re-resolves the configuration, and an acceptance task refuses with acceptance_reviewer_model_required. The goal therefore fails closed, but a review-bearing goal that cannot be used is saved.
findings.correction: In bind_review_model, drop existing `--model=` flags with blank values before appending the resolved `--model=<model>`, or refuse a blank explicit --model= with review_model_required.

findings.rule: behavior change: budget bounds on every review preparation
findings.evidence: prepare_feature_review now calls review_budget. A configured or explicit budget above 200000 (or an explicit one below 1000) is refused everywhere, including `validate --prepare-review` (probe big_ok_budget: exit 0 at HEAD, BLOCKED review_max_chars_out_of_bounds now). matches_commit also returns False for a receipt recorded at HEAD with max_chars above 200000. The 093 edge cases specify this and it fails closed. It is listed because existing projects with review_max_chars above 200000 will need a config change.
findings.correction: Optional: mention the new upper bound in the changelog or migration notes.
